messages.subject: Canopy C Matrix Construction
parts:
Hi Yuchao,

I was hoping you could answer some questions I had about how the CNA overlap matrix in Canopy should be created.
1) If CNAs are unique to different clones, but occupy a common position on the chromosome, should they be said to overlap?
2) The restriction that each CNA can be restricted to exactly one CNA region appears to make it impossible to evaluate CNAs that overlap twice. Is this indeed the case?
I have attached two diagrams to clarify these questions. Alternatively, if you have any diagrams showing the relationship between the C matrix, phylogeny, and CNA position, they would be very much appreciated.

Thank you for your help!

Best wishes,
William

messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Canopy C Matrix Construction
parts:
Hi William,

Thanks for your interest in Canopy and sorry for my late reply — I’ve been traveling and just got back to the States. For the two cases you sent in the slides, C.1 and C.3 are “more" correct whereas C.2 and C.4 don’t make sense. The overlapping CNA scenarios are not trivial and we tried to give an illustration and a “prototype” algorithm in the supplements of our paper. By saying “more” correct, I meant that the most ideal case is that you apply the prioritization algorithm to the three CNA events and get the CNA input for them respectively. In that case, you don’t need to define the overlapped regions as you did in C.2 and C.4 (and thus you don’t even need to define the C matrix). In essence, all that matters is to get the correct major and minor copy number input for the CNA EVENTS that are representative in the data. The easiest case is obviously to regard any overlapped regions and only use the regions that hit by one CNA only (that is, to remove region 2 and 4 in the second example of yours). The overlapped region method is to get CNA events in each region. The prioritization method is to get rid of the overlapped region notion and to get the correct copy number input from a correct region.

I would recommend going through Supplementary Figure S3 as well as the algorithm on page 2-3 in the supplements. We haven’t automated this pipeline yet but it is on our agenda. 

Hope that this clarifies. Feel free to let me know if you have more questions.

Cheers,
Yuchao
